title: October 3, 1978: a Kolkata doctor achieved the world's second-ever IVF birth - alone, with homemade equipment.

sources.text: ThePrint - Subhas Mukherjee pioneered IVF in India but the government refuted his work

caption:
October 3, 1978: a Kolkata doctor achieved the world's second-ever IVF birth - alone, with homemade equipment.

The baby, Kanupriya Agarwal, was the world's second IVF baby ever born, just 67 days after the UK's Louise Brown. Mukhopadhyay became only the second physician in the world - and the first in Asia - to achieve a live birth through in-vitro fertilization.

A state government committee dismissed his claim and barred him from presenting his work internationally. Professionally isolated, Mukhopadhyay died in 1981. It took until 2002 - 21 years after his death - for India's Council of Medical Research to formally recognize his pioneering achievement.

A Viksit Bharat by 2047 needs the institutions that recognize breakthroughs in time - not decades later. Mukhopadhyay's work now stands as one of India's earliest, least-celebrated contributions to reproductive medicine.
